set_aside.subject: classification of a per-file scratch-size limit hit
set_aside.text: “the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it, so the write fails with an error the code can see” conflicts with the later requirement that “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`)” decides `resource_exhausted`: the text does not say how `sandbox` learns that the scratch limit was hit when agent code catches the write error and returns normally
set_aside.question: What authoritative observation must `sandbox` use to classify a caught write past `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max` as `resource_exhausted`?
options: the runner records the kernel signal or failed write on its protected parent channel
a caught write error is not observable and the execution may otherwise succeed
the runner interposes file writes and records the limit hit
set_aside.default_guess: Have the in-sandbox runner record the limit event on its protected channel, like a trap hit, so catching the write error cannot hide `resource_exhausted`.
